AdditionalDetails.Value:
Outstanding Quality Clare Valley Riesling.
Intense lemon and lime citrus fruit.
Mineral acidity balanced with soft florals.
Region: Clare Valley, South Australia.
Colour: Pale straw with green hues.
Nose: Lifted, aromatic lime and citrus blossom.
Palate: Displaying excellent fruit definition, this is a classic example of Clare Riesling at its best. It displays the typical lime, citrus peel and talc notes of Clare Valley Rieslings, with great depth, good acid back bone with good length and intensity of flavour.
Oak: Unoaked.
Food Match: Moreton Bay bugs with a lemon and lime beurre blanc.
Winemaker: Matthew Reimann.
Drink Until: 2023.
Riesling is the most important grape for the Clare region and the Clare examples are some of the best the country produces. They have a tremendous ability to age - starting life in a fairly austere mode, with faint aromas of passionfruit, a touch of lime and a steely strength, then as the wine ages it develops the famous Riesling toast character and greater complexity and intensity. They can age for between 5 and 10 years, depending on the quality of the vintage.

The fruit is sourced from vineyards below the Italian Alps at elevations of around 300 to 450 metres above sea level on largely alluvial soils. Organic land management (with accreditation soon) and other sustainable projects focussing on renewable energy, zero-carbon emissions and recycling are employed. Santa Margherita pioneered pinot grigio during the 1960s and established a world-wide reputation for its fresh fruity and minerally pinot grigio style. Intense varietal expression and linear freshness epitomise modernity and versatility. Santa Margherita Pinot Grigio can be enjoyed as an aperitif or with a meal of many types, especially antipasto, seafood, pasta, chicken, veal and cheeses. AdditionalDetails.Value: 2021 Chalmers Vermentino is 100% Vermentino from the Chalmers vineyard in Heathcote on rich, red Cambrian soil, sitting 150-170m above sea level. Chalmers came out with Australia’s first Vermentino wine in 2004 and it’s since become a trademark line in the range, their ‘go-to’ white. There are now more than 100 winemakers working with the grape across this country and it’s no wonder when it loves the sunshine and makes such delicious wines with ultimate drinkability. Chalmers Vermentino is a truly unique iteration of the Mediterranean grape, a crisp and refreshing drink with white florals, soft stonefruit and a lick of saltiness, perfect for the Australian al fresco lifestyle. Handpicked fruit was whole bunch-pressed and wild fermented in stainless steel before the wine sat on less for 6 months. No acid adds. Vegan friendly. Clean and crisp, this Vermentino shows white peach and Meyer lemon with an overall chalkiness and sea spray tang leaving you wanting more.

AdditionalDetails.Value: Le Sauvignon Blanc by Paul Mas is the quintessential South of France experience where warm dry growing seasons lead to perfectly ripe grapes and gorgeously seductive wines. Vigneron Jean Claude Mas has worked assiduously to build a vineyard empire using organic and sustainable practices. A disciple of precision winemaking practices he employs the latest in technology to preserve natural fruit characters and linear freshness. The sauvignon blanc grapes are picked at optimum ripeness and cool-vinified at Domaine Paul Mas, near Pezenas in the Languedoc. Typically, this vibrant and juicy wine is pale coloured with intense grapefruit, lime, herb garden, camomile aromas, lovely fresh grapefruit, tropical fruit, lemon curd flavours, fine lacy textures and superb cutting acidity. The silk screened “flower” bottle neatly captures and sells the floral aromatics and prettiness of the wine. This is very much a warmer climate style with plenty of expression, freshness and flavour. Enjoy as a sundowner or pair with summer salads, roast chicken or pork, or seafood dishes.

AdditionalDetails.Value: Made from one of the oldest Languedoc grapes, Belardent is an outstanding white wine from the Mediterranean sea shores. Carefully crafted according to Appellation winemaking specification, it also benefits from the winemaking history of its production area. Refreshing, it has lovely aromas of citrus and mineral flavours that will get along perfectly with seafood delights! The Picpoul de Pinet winegrowing area runs along the southern French coast, separated from the waves of the Mediterranean only by the Etang de Thau. This lagoon is France’s second largest lake. Harboured by the town of Sète, it is famous for its delicious oysters that are the perfect combination for a Picpoul Pinet. The Picpoul de Pinet terroir consists of a triangle bounded by Agde, Pézenas and Sète : a limestone plateau basking in the rising sun covered with highly perfumed garrigue, rows of vines, and scattered pine groves. Thanks to its terroir, the region produces mineral wines with lovely and refreshing citrus aromas.<br>Produced by LGI Wines and imported by Pinnacle Drinks, part of Endeavour Group Limited.

AdditionalDetails.Value: Lovely pale yellow colour with green tints. Lifted Sauvignon Blanc aromas with green fruit, citrus pith and florals in the background. Initial flavours of citrus and melon, light cool palate at 11.5% alcohol. Grapefruit, finger lime and a zesty acidity adds to the structure. A perfect summer drink paired with a wide range of food. We’re quite proud to introduce this wine, the 33rd vintage of the blend. The label didn’t get the full Cricket Pitch livery until the 1995 vintage, although the Cabernet Sauvignon,Merlot was labelled as Cricket Pitch for the 1991 vintage. This wine is a blend of 81% Sauvignon Blanc and 19% Semillon. Due to the late vintage in the eastern states, multiple South Eastern Australian growing regions make up this blend, with the majority from New South Wales and South Australia. This wine also highlights our desire for lower alcohol and weighs in at 11.5% and with plenty of zesty fruit lift. We are fortunate enough to be able to process almost all of the grapes here in the Hunter Valley, enabling an extra level of winemaker attention. This ensures the delicate grape aromas are preserved. Fermentation in 100% stainless steel tanks.

Kendall Jackson Vintners Reserve Chardonnay is an enduring symbol of the chardonnay revolution and has a history going back nearly fifty years with the establishment of cool-climate vineyards on California’s Central Coast. The style has been refined over the years but the essence remains the same. The wine is typically richly flavoured and supple with fresh white peach nectarine grilled nut aromas, lovely mid-palate creaminess, underlying vanilla toasted hazelnut notes and long fresh integrated acidity. This Californian style is ample yet minerally with attractive fruit sweetness. Barrel ferment characters and French oak maturation give the wine an extra layer of complexity and fine lacy textures. This is a great retro-modern style that will appeal to drinkers who like volume, flavour, oak, freshness and balance! Pair with grilled fish or prawns, roast chicken, mushroom risotto or vegetable terrine.
Produced by Jackson Family Wines and imported by Pinnacle Drinks, part of Endeavour Group Limited.

AdditionalDetails.Value: Perfect, pale green colour and lifted grapefruit aromas. The French oak sits nicely with the fine, juicy citrus flavours on the palate accompanied by subtle bran meal. The driving force of this wine is the acidity – long and pure. More than three quarters from Beechworth, the balance being from a combination of the Hunter Valley, Yarra Valley and Orange. The final components of this wine basically selected themselves. Another top-notch vintage! A milder and later than average growing season was the dominant factor in Beechworth for vintage 2022. Above average rainfall throughout 2021 made for a challenging growing season with disease pressure a constant. January was wet, with 140mm falling for the month. Thankfully the rain cleared for February, allowing the vineyard to dry off. The fruit was picked before a second deluge arrived in early March, with the fruit in good condition with fine acidity. Brokenwood, along with a large number of Chardonnay producers, are harvesting much earlier than 15 years ago. This is partly due to a lot of vineyards reaching maturity, and therefore having great fruit flavour and concentration at lower sugar levels. Additionally, consumers are demanding more finely structured Chardonnay, meaning lower alcohols and less oak.

AdditionalDetails.Value: The family behind DBR Lafite has been producing wine in Bordeaux since 1868. Their understanding of Bordeaux has been culminating over six generations, driven by the purpose of allowing wine lovers all over the world to be able to dive into the originality of the varied appellations and terroirs with confidence. DBR Lafite is also B-Corp certified, demonstrating their commitment to environmental and social responsibility.The wines of the Saga R range serve as the reference point of each appellation, with a focus on expressing the freshness and elegance that make Bordeaux great. The fruit for Saga R Bordeaux Blanc is sourced from east-facing limestone slopes in the Entre-Deux-Mers region, renowned for its crisp, lively dry white wines. The blend of 90% Sauvignon Blanc and 10% Semillon is harvested in the cool of the night and fermented at low temperature in stainless steel to maintain freshness, acidity, and aromatics.Pale straw yellow in appearance with aromatics, floral notes of lilies and white flowers, and white peach, green pineapple and lychee. Round and balanced with excellent freshness and crispness on the finish. Brilliant on its own as an aperitif, or with fish, oysters, and white meats.

AdditionalDetails.Name: webdescriptionshort
AdditionalDetails.Value: Lime Blossom. Bosch Pear. Floral. Textured. These grapes were harvested in the early hours of the morning and pressed upon arrival at the winery. The lightly pressed juice was cold settled and racked with light solids for fermentation. Fermentation of the juice took place in both stainless steel and neutral barrels with regular stirring. The skin contact component representing approximately 15% of the blend was plunged twice daily and then basket pressed half way through fermentation at the ideal texture and tannin balance, which occurred after 12 days. A blend of 15pct Skin Contact and 85 pct Oak and Stainless Ferment was made shortly after ferment and then transferred to neutral barrels, amphora and concrete on light lees. Regular stirring took place throughout the maturation of 6 months in oak and concrete. Blended in September to prepare for bottling.

AdditionalDetails.Name: webdescriptionshort
AdditionalDetails.Value: A blend of fresh aromatic whites, with notes of citrus blossom, dusky rose petal, and pear skin, set in a texturally rich palate that finishes savoury, chalky and mineral. All varieties were allowed to ripen to an extent where they express the full array of ripe flavours. After the hand harvest, the variety is gently pressed to extract juice for fermentation in 600lt demi muid oak and 400 lt ceramic eggs. Some intact bunches are added to the Gewurztraminer and Sauvignon Blanc egg ferments to infuse wild berry skin and green mango skin notes into the developing wines. Each variety remains in the same vessels for ten months, with occasional stirring to suspend yeast lees, build texture, and freshen the maturing wine. The wine was minimally fined after blending, filtered, and bottled in late December 2022.

AdditionalDetails.Value: Some wines are made for quiet contemplation. GA-LOR-IA! is not one of them. Born from McLaren Vale's sun-drenched soils, this effervescent Sangiovese Grenache is a love letter to spontaneity - a wine that fizzes with as much personality as it does with bubbles. Winemaker Mary Hamilton knew which parcels belonged together from the moment of pressing, but it took many months of trials to find the missing ingredient: a light frizzante splash of gas that gave the blend its essential spark of playfulness. Pink ladies mingle on a savoury stage with cherry pit, raspberry seeds, and a whisper of strawberry lip gloss. The palate is a spectacular fruit-filled centre wrapped in elegant effervescence - talc-textured, full, and bracingly fresh. Built to build appetite and beg for good company. Serve well-chilled alongside aperitif bites or carry it to the nearest picnic rug and let the afternoon take care of itself. All-singing, all-dancing McLaren Vale joy in a glass. Vegan friendly. Drink now.

AdditionalDetails.Value: Well, we made a cool wine, from one of the hottest and driest vintages, from one of Australia’s hottest wine regions. Pretty snazzy eh? Combine this with being dry grown, it gives us confidence our little region has a few more miles under the bonnet for the bumpy road of climate change ahead. 100% Chenin Blanc grown on Rocket’s Vineyard in Upper Swan. Soils are Houghton loam and the clones are Noack massale selection. The vines are planted at a density of 1540 vines per hectare. The grapes were picked on 16th and 22nd January 2020. Bottled on 11th November 2020 Alcohol 13%; RS 0.8g/L; pH 3.32; total Acidity 5.78g/L. The grapes were harvested by hand and whole bunch-pressed prior to natural fermentation. A portion was fermented and matured in seasoned French oak barriques for seven months prior to blending and bottling. The wine smells of lemon pith and nashi pear with a lick of carbide. The palate is lively with a briny spine, great clarity and stacks of flavour. – Rob and Gen Mann

AdditionalDetails.Value: At release, the wine is a very pale straw colour with a slight green tinge to the edge. The wine exhibits complex aromas of zesty lemon and lime aromas along with delightful orange blossom and faint rosewater characters. Across the palate, the wine is exceptionally balanced with an abundance of lemon and lime juice characters and a hint of fresh rose petals and white ginger. There is a crisp and refreshing lime acidity through the mid-palate leading to a finish of superb persistence. The growing season leading into vintage 2024 started with a relatively dry and slightly warmer than average winter. Spring weather was consistent with long term averages and budburst occurred on track in early September. There were some minor frost events recorded in September but damage was minimal. At the end of October, however, the Clare Valley recorded a significant frost event which affected yields. The fruit that was able to be harvested however was of exceptionally high quality. Crafted for immediate enjoyment but will cellar over a long term under ideal conditions.

AdditionalDetails.Value: Onannon is a three-man team comprising close mates Sam Middleton and Kaspar Hermann (both of Mount Mary), and Will Byron of Stonier. This is 100% 95 clone Chardonnay from a single site in Tuerong. Fruit is crushed into the press, after which it's settled overnight and then racked to barrel. The Onannon team played around with different levels of solids, and a combination of yeasts was used to help build complexity. No MLF. 20% new French oak, 10 months in barrel. The nose is smoky with grilled hazelnut, nectarine and ghee. It has a very tight, clean attack, a pure soda/mineral mid-palate. It's more delicate than the '16 with better oak integration and finishes with clean, chewy savouriness and lively length.

Founded in 1933 Cave de Tain is located at the foot of the hill of Hermitage between Valencia and Lyon. The historic property is a local co-op (one of the best in France) with over 300 grower-members and 1000 hectares of vineyards making it the main producer of wines in Northern Rhône Valley.

Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin is one of Burgundy’s most prestigious family-owned houses. Now led by the fourth generation, the estate is defined by a signature style of effortless elegance. Their 100-hectare domain is farmed entirely using organic and biodynamic practices, spanning the region's most iconic Grand Cru and Premier Cru plots. From the legendary Montrachet Marquis de Laguiche to their accessible regional classics, Drouhin wines are celebrated for their purity, finesse, and true terroir character.
Joseph Drouhin’s Bourgogne Chardonnay offers an expressive bouquet of citrus, peach, and delicate white flowers. Matured in a combination of stainless steel and oak barrels, it achieves a harmonious balance between fruit purity and a silky, textured palate. A bright line of acidity carries the wine into a crisp, mineral-inflected finish. Accessible and vibrant, this blend of different vineyard plots from across Burgundy captures the authentic character of the region and is the perfect gateway to Burgundy.

This pioneering spirit still rings true after nearly two centuries and is what has helped them become one of the most celebrated winemakers in the world today. In true Bin 311 style, not unlike Yattarna, it exhibits lemon lime aromas and a mineral acid backbone, complemented by barrel fermentation and maturation in new and seasoned oak. AdditionalDetails.Name: webdescriptionshort
AdditionalDetails.Value:
Kooyong Estate Chardonnay comprises fruit from our Faultline and Farrago blocks. It offers an overall expression of the Kooyong vineyard, with parcels of fruit from various soils and mesoclimates blended together to create the Estate label. Year after year the same parcels are consistenltly chosen, giving this wine an underlying likeness across vintages. The grapes were gently whole-bunchpressed directly into French oak barriques (21% of which were new) where fermentation occured spontaneously with ambient yeasts. Following fermentation, the wine was aged on lees (without battonage) for 11 month . It was bottled without fining and with minimal filtration.

The vibrant and intriguing nose offers fresh grapefruit citrus that merges to white pear with a hint of peel, together with struck flint, creamy nougat and a comlpexing note of dried spice. The palate is poised and driven, displaying bright lemon and grapefruit citrus flavours entwined with a creamy lees texture from barrel fermetation. The acid line is fine and long providing vibrancy and freshness through the palate with a tale-like grip. Although drinking well now the wine will benefit from further cellaring in the medium term.

Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin is one of Burgundy’s most prestigious family-owned houses. Now led by the fourth generation, the estate is defined by a signature style of effortless elegance. Their 100-hectare domain is farmed entirely using organic and biodynamic practices, spanning the region's most iconic Grand Cru and Premier Cru plots. From the legendary Montrachet Marquis de Laguiche to their accessible regional classics, Drouhin wines are celebrated for their purity, finesse, and true terroir character.
The Montagny Premier Cru reveals a bouquet of golden apple, lemon curd, fresh almond, and white flowers. The palate is bright and citrus-led with a silky roundness. Aged for 12–14 months in French oak, with just a touch of new wood, it is a pure, expressive wine that maintains its freshness while offering layers of subtle complexity. A stellar representation of the Côte Chalonnaise, it delivers the prestige of a Burgundy Premier Cru at a more accessible price point than its neighbors in the Côte de Beaune.

The Frescobaldi Castello Pomino estate dates back to the year 1500, when the castle of the same name was built here in the Florentine mountains. It was identified by Grand Duke Cosimo III de'Medici as far back as 1716 as an exceptional area for the production of wines, alongside areas such as Chianti, Carmignano, and Val d'Arno di Sopra. At an altitude of 700 metres above sea level, the cooler conditions are ideal for growing fine and complex Chardonnay.

The Benefizio Cru first came into being in 1973 as the first white wine in Italy to be fermented and aged in oak barriques. The current oak regime is 50% new and 50% first fill, with partial malolactic fermentation and occasional lees stirring.

The resulting wine is a pale straw-yellow in appearance. Complex and intriguing on the nose, with exotic notes of mango, white peach, toasted cashews and hints of freshly churned butter. Creamy and textural on the palate, with well-judged, moreish notes of toasty oak. A beautifully layered wine.

Founded in 1880, Maison Joseph Drouhin is one of Burgundy’s most prestigious family-owned houses. Now led by the fourth generation, the estate is defined by a signature style of effortless elegance. Their 100-hectare domain is farmed entirely using organic and biodynamic practices, spanning the region's most iconic Grand Cru and Premier Cru plots. From the legendary Montrachet Marquis de Laguiche to their accessible regional classics, Drouhin wines are celebrated for their purity, finesse, and true terroir character.
The Côte de Beaune Blanc is crafted from declassified young vines within Drouhin’s prestigious Premier Cru vineyards, including the iconic Clos des Mouches. Fresh and aromatic, this vibrant white offers an inviting medley of lemon zest and crisp green apple, underpinned by undertones of white flowers and fresh almond. Aged 12–14 months in French oak with 10–15% new oak, it blends a supple, round texture with a stony, saline-driven finish that provides excellent lift. A rare find that punches far above its weight and offers a unique window into Burgundy’s Premier Cru terroirs at a village-level classification.

Jean Noel Gagnard handed his eponymous Domaine to his daughter Caroline Lestimé in 1989. She had studied business in Paris, before returning to the village to take over the reins of the family estate, and had to handle male chauvinism at its most rampant. Nonetheless, she has followed her own convictions, and enhanced (rather than diminished) the reputation of this fine producer. In the vineyard, she uses no fertilisers or herbicides, but has not taken hold of the biodynamic bible.- James Halliday.
Gagnard's daughter Caroline Lestimé’s 0.34ha plot, formerly Pinot Noir, was replanted in 1990 to Chardonnay. The vineyard faces south-east at 250m altitude, half-way up a moderately-steep slope of stony clay over limestone blocks. Viticulture is certified organic and biodynamic. Hand-picked grapes undergo a delicate pneumatic pressing before 24 to 48 hours static settling in tank followed by indigenous yeast alcoholic and malolactic fermentation in 228 litre oak barrels at 18°C. The wine matures for 18 months aging on lees in barrels (30-35% new) at 10-12°C.

AdditionalDetails.Value: "93-94 points, William Kelley, The Wine Advocate, January 2025 The 2023 Beaune 1er Cru Clos des Mouches Blanc (Domaine) is another strong performance, delivering aromas of sweet pear, peach and mandarin mingled with buttered toast and mint. Full-bodied, rich and ample, it's layered and unctuous, with a seamless, satiny, textural profile and a long, lusty finish. 92-94 points, Neal Martin, Vinous.com, November 2024 The 2023 Beaune Clos des Mouches Blanc 1er Cru has more intensity on the nose than expected, with lovely lilting yellow fruit, quince and crushed stone scents. The palate is very well balanced and generous, with a slightly oily texture, great depth, fine acidity and a judicious touch of lemongrass toward the finish that feels long and intense. This may well surpass the 2022. 92-95 points, Jasper Morris, November 2024 Mid lemon, with the somewhat more sumptuous bouquet of Clos des Mouches, always more flesh right from the outset. This is a powerful fleshy wine, with a good oak support, probably higher in alcohol. Lower than expected yield here in white. May well be around 14% I suspect but that goes with this territory. Drink from 2029-2038. Tasted Nov 2024. 94 points, Charles Curtis MW, Decanter.com Drouhin's Clos des Mouches 2023 exemplifies the vintage's potential for delicious whites. The wine has lush, forward aromas of Mirabelle plums and quince with hints of marzipan, butter and a suggestion of stylishly smoky reduction. The texture is supple and dense, but the richness is kept in balance and the extract carries the wine to a lingering finish. Parts of the 7ha vineyard have been replanted; the old vines that produce this bottling have delivered a wine of great character. 95 points, Tim Atkin, Jamuary 2025 Honeyed with sweet spices and toasted brioche on the nose, the suavely crafted mouthfeel glows with perfectly ripe fruit. Yellow cherries, starfruit, golden kiwi and feijoa deliver excellent complexity. The light, pleasant baby fat in the mid-palate is gently hemmed in by supporting acidity. This is another seamless Clos des Mouches, which seems to reach new heights each year. The Drouhin's 14 hectares of Clos des Mouches are evenly split between white and red plantings with six hectares of each currently in production."
